stories.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Opus 5, its new flagship model
stories.blurb: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, the next generation of its top-tier model. The company says it outperforms the previous flagship across coding, math, and complex reasoning tasks, with improved speed and longer context handling.
stories.why_it_matters: The bar for what counts as state-of-the-art just moved again.

stories.headline: Claude's voice mode now works with its smartest models
stories.blurb: Anthropic's voice mode previously only ran on Haiku, its fastest but least capable model. Now you can talk to Claude's more powerful Opus and Sonnet models, and the feature works inside Gmail, Slack, and Canva.
stories.why_it_matters: Voice conversations just got smarter — you can now speak to Claude's best reasoning models, not just the quick one.
stories.original_headline: Claude’s voice mode is now available for Opus and Sonnet

stories.headline: Meta AI can now check your calendar and write daily briefings
stories.blurb: Meta is adding productivity features to its chatbot to compete with ChatGPT and Claude. The update lets Meta AI access your calendar to help plan events, generate daily briefings, and do research you can guide in real time.
stories.why_it_matters: Meta's free chatbot is becoming an actual productivity tool instead of just a search engine.
stories.original_headline: Meta is making its AI chatbot more like an assistant

stories.headline: Cursor now picks the best AI model for every coding task
stories.blurb: Cursor's new Router system automatically chooses which AI model to use for each coding request in Auto mode. Instead of you deciding between Claude, GPT-4, or other models, Cursor analyzes your task and routes it to whichever model is most likely to solve it well.
stories.why_it_matters: You get better code suggestions without learning which model works best for what.

try_this_prompt.prompt: I'm preparing for a negotiation I'll describe below. Don't coach me on tactics. try_this_prompt.tool_hint: Before you walk into the room thinking you've got all the angles.
